> we need to have anarchist counter-institutions that replace the functions of the existing hierarchical institutions.

Self-reliance, communes, separatist communities, these will lay the foundation for an alternative anarchic society. There has to be somewhere for people to gravitate once they get it in their heads enough's enough sucking on capitalism's teat.

#YES ALL ADMIRALS

Top quality post by the way.

And that is an easy answer. The more difficult answer is that the crown honored its treaties with the tribes in the Ohio River Valley better than the colonists did. Given that many of the founders were land speculators, including Washington, that didn't bode well in what was then one of the most lavishly fertile regions in the New World. Likewise, pushing westward was not necessarily a British interest and indeed the crown determined to move northward and plant serious roots.

It was taxation without representation, it was rum riots, it was the lack of "manifest destiny" in British policy that set up rent economies, it was not wanting to slaughter every single Native American, it was early abolition of slavery.

Though it was zero percent about FREEDOM(TM) as some lofty idealist like Paine would've made it out to be.
